note: The Democrat of 1835-07-29, Vol. II No. 15, read through — the last issue of the scene month and the richest of the four in NEW matter. Read from the committed derived text, which resolves on `dev`, so every quote is machine-checked on this branch. WHAT IS NEW HERE and nowhere else in the range: a second auction and commission house opening in a new store on Dearborn Street (c004), a good store standing empty and to let in John T. Temple's gift (c003), millwrights wanted (c005), a fifty-dollar note repudiated (c002), and the only vessel list in the four issues whose arrival DATES survive the transcription (c001). Everything else is the scene month's standing advertising in its last printing, recorded where a second witness settles something the first could not — Cooley and Halsman's anchor is the Eagle COFFEE House (c009), Kinzie's hams are Ohio hams (c007), Wm. Hogue & Co.'s third partner is WM. HOGUE whole (c010), and Russell E. Heacock's name is legible here where his address was legible on 1835-07-08 (c018). THE GRAIN: the docx rebuild delivers half-columns as single lines of up to 6,926 characters, so most claims here are cut with `locator.spans`. NO CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST: swept for every form the Democrat uses, for one hit, the Juliet return of 1 July 1835 reprinted from 1835-07-22 (page 4 column 2, line 497) and not minted, under T-0299.

Montgomery's rooms on South Water Street were the town's auction house on 1 July 1835, and this is a competitor arriving four weeks later.

claims.notes: THE WITNESS THAT CARRIES THE NAME, where the deposit printing carries the address — the two halves of one standing advertisement, and the reason chicago_democrat_1835_07_08 c012 could be made at all. The 1835-07-08 crop sheared the heading to '• E. ,' and kept 'Office in the 2d story, opposite the Exchange, corner of Lake and Franklin-sts'; this one keeps 'RUSSELL FE. HEACOCK, | Counsetior asd Attorney at Law' and loses the address to the same crop from the other side. The two are the same advertisement — the body matches phrase for phrase down to 'having been a resident at Chicago for the last eight years' and 'the first 30 miles of the Illinois canal line' — which is why the person is minted here and the placement is recorded there. THIS CLAIM'S OWN PLACEMENT CLASS IS `none`, because this quote places nobody; the corner is the other claim's evidence and is not restated as if this one carried it. 'FE.' is read as 'E.' — the Chicago attorney and justice of the peace of that name is Russell E. Heacock, and the middle initial is single in the other printing's own body.
